_README: EXAMPLE CONFIG — a template, not a working ruleset. Replace every rule below with
your own before relying on it. The rules that ship here are illustrations of the
shape; they protect nothing.
Substitutions applied when exporting a wiki node for a reader outside your team.
The principle: the wiki keeps your team's real language; the EXPORT adapts to its
audience. Never edit the source to suit an outside reader — change this file instead.
A record you sanitise as you write it is a record you can no longer trust.
`rules` are applied IN ORDER (regex source in `find`). Order matters: a phrase rule
must be able to pre-empt a word rule over the same term. Prefer phrase rules when the
surrounding sentence would become false after a bare word swap — e.g. a sentence that
explains why a name was chosen stops being true when the name changes.
`forbidden` is the fail-closed check. After the rules run, the export REFUSES to emit
if any of these still match. It is matched case-insensitively regardless of how the
rules were written, so it can disagree with the rules rather than merely agree. That
disagreement is the point: a check that can only confirm the rules cannot catch them
being wrong.
Adding a term to `forbidden` without a matching rule will (correctly) break the export.
⚠️ Note what this file becomes once you fill it in: a list of the things you consider
sensitive, in one place, in plain text. It is itself the most revealing file in your
checkout. Keep your filled-in copy out of any repository you publish.
⚠️ Beware terms that collide with your own roster. A forbidden entry matching a name
you legitimately use will refuse every export that mentions that person.

rules.note: EXAMPLE — phrase rule. Must run before the word rule below. Use this shape when a bare word swap would leave the surrounding sentence making a false claim about the term.
rules.find: the mode is called `local-name` because of an in-joke nobody outside the team will get
rules.replace: the mode is called `token-ring`: a single lease is passed seat to seat around a fixed ring, and only its holder may speak.

rules.note: EXAMPLE — word-level mop-up for any remaining occurrence, after the phrase rules have had their turn.
EXAMPLE — internal nickname to a neutral one. Pick a replacement in the same register as your other names, so a reader glides past it instead of stopping to wonder.
EXAMPLE — a real commit hash from a private repository. Carries no meaning for an outside reader; costs nothing to neutralise.

forbidden.note: absolute path leaking a local username — worth keeping
